newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NO PLANS TO STOP SELLING BEER IN BURMA - INTERBREW.
newsitem.headline: NO PLANS TO STOP SELLING BEER IN BURMA - INTERBREW.

text.p: Belgium's privately owned Interbrew NV, the fourth largest brewer in the world, said on Friday it would not direct distributors to stop selling its beers in Burma so as to observe a call for an economic boycott.

Responding to a Belgian media report that Interbrew was breaking the boycott, Interbrew spokesman Gerard Fauchey said: "We didn't know there was an economic boycott of Burma and if so we'd like to know who proclaimed it".

Earlier this year brewers Heineken and Carlsberg stopped selling beers, and investing, in Burma after calls by human rights groups and Burmese opposition leader and 1991 Nobel Peace Prize winner, Aung San Suu Kyi, for foreign companies to boycott the military dictatorship in Burma.
"We don't see any reason why we shouldn't continue," he said, "We sell (beers) in about 100 countries and we have no control over where our distributors sell our beer."
He said one of its distributors, a Japanese trading company operating from Singapore, had sold 500 hectolitres of its Labatt Ice beer in Burma.
"Interbrew does not invest in Burma and we have no intention of selling beer (there) directly," Fauchey added.
He noted that "it's very difficult to take into account everything that happens with human rights action groups around the world."
Interbrew became the world's fourth largest brewer when it bought Canadian brewing group John Labatt Ltd in a $2 billion takeover in July last year.

It has operations in Belgium, Canada, the UK, France, the Netherlands, Hungary, Croatia, Romania, Bulgaria, and the Ukraine, and joint ventures in the U.S., China, the Philippines and the Dominican Republic.
